{{Quote|Squibs. They'll sell you a bucket of air if you let them, and keep the bucket.|[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]|<ref name="TG">''[[Tatooine Ghost]]''</ref>}}
'''Squibs''' were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] from [[Skor II]] known for collecting, trading, and haggling. Adult Squibs had [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] bodies that averaged a [[Meter/Legends|meter]] in height. They were covered in [[Color/Legends|colorful]] [[Hair/Legends|fur]] and had pointed snouts, tufted [[Ear/Legends|ears]], and large [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]. Squibs tasted objects by rubbing them over their fur. They were gregarious, insatiably curious, and obsessed with haggling and deal-making. It was said that the easiest way to get information from a Squib was to propose a trade.

Skor II was rich in natural resources, but they were unevenly distributed. As the Squibs developed the compulsion to collect and stockpile baubles, some tribes settled down while others became nomadic [[Merchant/Legends|traders]]. Over [[Time/Legends|time]], a complex system of trade and barter emerged. After their first contact with [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] at large, the Squibs established themselves as [[Galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Scavenger/Legends|scavengers]] and rivals to the [[Ugor/Legends|Ugors]], another species. [[King/Legends|King]] [[Ebareebaveebeedee]], who vocally supported the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] during the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]], struck agreements with galactic interests to place Squibs aboard [[Capital ship/Legends|capital spacecraft]] as laborers. The [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] considered such Squibs [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]], but they provided salvage [[Starship/Legends|vessels]] with the locations of Imperial dumpsites. The species later signed a [[Unidentified Squib pact|pact of mutual support]] with the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]].

Squib salvagers reclaimed, refurbished, and resold rubbish both [[Planet/Legends|planetside]] and deep in [[Realspace/Legends|space]]. Many worked directly for a corporation known as the [[Squib Merchandising Consortium]], while others operated independently. Although most stayed within the law, some found work as [[Forger (profession)/Legends|forgers]], thieves, and even [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lords]]. The [[Solo family/Legends|Solo family]] had several encounters with the Squibs [[Emala]], [[Grees]], and [[Sligh]], a family unit who operated as [[Black market/Legends|black market]] art dealers and [[Information broker/Legends|information brokers]].

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|You're like a nexu! One color when you're a baby, another when you're grown up!|[[Allana Djo Solo|Allana Solo]], on the dappled fur of a growing Squib|<ref name="Asc" />}}
[[File:Squib_Alien_Anthology.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Squibs could rotate their tufted ears to hone in on faint sounds.]]
Squibs were small, [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]], [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]]<ref name="GG4" /> [[Mammal/Legends|mammals]]<ref name="AE" /> with both [[Rodent/Legends|rodent]]<ref name="TSW" /> and [[Canine/Legends|canine]] characteristics.<ref name="NRRG">{{WEGCite|story=New Recruits and Rebel Guns|book=Instant Adventures}}</ref> They ranged from 0.8 to 1.2 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in height<ref name="UAA" /> and weighed twenty-two [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]] on average.<ref name="TUR" /> Their [[Color/Legends|pink]] skin was covered in [[Hair/Legends|fur]]<ref name="TTWS" /> that ranged from white,<ref name="UAA" /> gray,<ref name="GG7" /> black, and brown<ref name="TSW" /> to blue,<ref name="GG4" /> violet,<ref name="OE" /> and red.<ref name="GG4" /> The coat offered some protection from cold weather,<ref name="Asc" /> but, more importantly, it served as an olfactory organ, able to pick up scents at a distance<ref name="SP">{{JournalCite|11|Spare Parts (short story)}}</ref> and ascertain intrinsic details&mdash;such as penetrating through a disguise<ref name="TSW" /> or identifying a forgery<ref name="TG" />&mdash;when rubbed against.<ref name="GG4" /> The species included male and female [[Gender/Legends|genders]], although non-Squibs often had difficulty determining them based on appearances alone.<ref name="TG" />

Squib [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] were large in relation to the [[Skeleton/Legends|skull]] and located on the sides of the head.<ref name="GG4" /> They came in shades of blue,<ref name="OE" /> yellow, red,<ref name="GG4" /> and brown.<ref name="TTWS" /> Their large [[Ear/Legends|ears]] often sported tufts of fur whose color could differ from that of the main coat;<ref name="OE" /> the ears pointed upward<ref name="SH" /> and could pivot to zero in on specific sounds.<ref name="UAA" /> The short Squib muzzle<ref name="SH" /> tapered to a bewhiskered<ref name="TSW" /> black [[Nose/Legends|nose]].<ref name="GG4" /> Their [[Mouth/Legends|mouths]] were full of forbidding, sharp, white [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]],<ref name="Asc" /> and their flexible cheeks were capable of storing items.<ref name="TG" /> The [[Species/Legends|species]] had nimble, five-fingered hands and five toes on each foot.<ref name="GG4" /> Non-Squibs often considered the small beings humorous<ref name="TUR" /> or cute in appearance.<ref name="Ap" />

The Squibs had quick metabolisms<ref name="DB Squib">{{DB|species|squib|Squib}}</ref> and relatively short life spans. A Squib was considered a [[Youngling/Legends|child]]&mdash;referred to as a ''fuzzling''<ref name="SP" />&mdash;until nine [[Standard year/Legends|standard years]] of age.<ref name="UAA" /> As he or she matured, the fur changed color, a phenomenon that caused a dappled appearance on the back;<ref name="Asc" /> similarly, the eyes<ref name="Ap" /> and ears grew more quickly than the rest of the body, causing the latter to flop until the rest of the fuzzling's body grew enough to catch up.<ref name="Asc" /> Sexual maturity occurred at thirteen standard years. Beginning at around thirty-nine years, a Squib entered middle age,<ref name="UAA" /> when the fur grayed and the face wrinkled.<ref name="SH" /> Squib life expectancy was about sixty-five standard years.<ref name="UAA" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|Dibs on the big pieces!''"''<br />''"''Eat hot trash, Ugorian slime!''"''<br />''"''Death to all single-minded fanatics of Ugor!|Squib crew of ''Thrifty''|<ref name="SH" />}}
[[File:Annoying_Squib.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Squibs accumulated large collections of what others considered junk.]]
Squibs were cheerful, gregarious, and overconfident to the point of egotism.<ref name="GG4" /> Their biology led to a common Squib greeting: rubbing a person's palm across the cheek fur. As Squibs often wore [[Glove/Legends|gloves]], the gesture conveyed more information than a simple handshake.<ref name="Tatooine Ghost">''[[Tatooine Ghost]]'', describes this greeting; images of gloved Squibs appear in ''[[Heroes & Rogues]]'', ''[[Alien Anthology]]'', and ''[[Rookies: Rendezvous]]''</ref> They were friendly and non-threatening, making them quite likable&mdash;at first. Over time, Squib acquaintances could grow to regard the beings as slightly annoying to downright obnoxious;<ref name="GG4" /> over many encounters, the Human [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] came to strongly dislike the species, for instance.<ref name="INV">''[[Legacy of the Force: Invincible]]''</ref> [[List of phrases and slang/Legends|''Furbag'']]<ref name="TUQ">''[[Dark Nest II: The Unseen Queen]]''</ref> and ''furball'' were derisive terms for Squibs.<ref name="RNTB">''[[Rookies: No Turning Back]]''</ref>

Squibs were inherently curious. They handled anything that interested them, usually by rubbing it against their fur with little forethought as to whether doing so might be harmful.<ref name="GG4" /> Squib curiosity and propensity for haggling made them unabashed pack rats. Although the species had no need for [[Clothing/Legends|clothing]] to protect themselves from the elements, they wore clothes and footwear for reasons of appearance and extra storage;<ref name="Asc" /> typical clothing included pockets and pouches to stuff with odds and ends that caught their eye, since a Squib could never tell when a particular item might be useful in making a deal.<ref name="SH" /> Still, individuals left fur exposed to facilitate olfaction.<ref name="UAA" /> Their accumulative drives earned the species a reputation as thieves among some members of the [[galactic community]].<ref name="TJP">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref>

Cheerful overconfidence was a definitive trait. The typical Squib response to a threat was not to fight or flee, but to bluff and bluster. Such behavior was particularly evident when the Squibs were out of sight, as when communicating from a Squib [[Starship/Legends|spacecraft]].<ref name="SH" /> However, their sharp teeth were a favored means of intimidation when they felt such a tactic was necessary.<ref name="FP">{{GamerCite|1|Fair Prey}}</ref>

Squibs were known for resourcefulness<ref name="TG" /> and improvisation.<ref name="SH" /> The traits manifested themselves in both Squib technology and art. For example, many Squibs sported homemade [[Ion blaster/Legends|ion blasters]], cobbled together from spare parts, which they used to disable [[Droid/Legends|droids]] they wished to reclaim.<ref name="Arms & Equipment Guide">''[[Arms & Equipment Guide]]''</ref> Squib artists utilized found objects&mdash;i.e., garbage&mdash;which they organized into intricate and beautiful works.<ref name="H&R">''[[Heroes & Rogues]]''</ref> For example, the audience chamber on the Squib [[Momship]] ''[[Thrifty]]'' featured a [[Unidentified mural (Squib craft)|mural]] of Squib craft, [[Unidentified mural (Paradise system)|one]] of the collapse of the [[Paradise system/Legends|Paradise system]], and [[Unidentified mural (Rebel operatives)|another]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] [[operative]]s who helped to bring it about.<ref name="SH" />

===Haggling===
{{Quote|Got nice go-go vehicle here, pal, still work good, sorta, but it's a classic. Trade for new talkie-talk shiny man. Good deal. Wanna trade?|A Squib trader|<ref name="H&R" />}}
[[File:Squib_trader.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Squibs traded from planet to planet in the tradition of their nomadic ancestors.]]
To Squibs, bargaining was an art form. The highest compliment one could pay a Squib was that he or she bargained well,<ref name="SH" /> and a Squib denied the chance to haggle for any length of time could grow withdrawn and melancholy.<ref name="COL">"[[Child of Light]]"</ref> Some members of the species claimed to have trained in the [[Mystic Martial Arts of Squib Combats and Transactions]],<ref name="H&R" /> and the species celebrated a holiday called [[Haggleday]].<ref name="The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia II-6">{{CSWECite|II|6|Haggleday}}</ref> Haggling was superior to all other impulses, and the Squibs were experts at it.<ref name="SH" />

Squib bargaining followed three major rules: 1: If something was free, it was a good deal; 2: bargaining was the highest form of communication; 3: when dealing with the Squibs' nemeses, the [[Ugor/Legends|Ugors]], all bets were off. Still, a few other principles applied. First, Squibs preferred to bargain face to face.<ref name="SH" /> Such a scenario allowed them to play up their small, unassuming appearance and make their opponent feel overconfident.<ref name="GG4" /> Next, by tradition, the party who wanted something&mdash;usually the Squib&mdash;had to make the first offer. The furry beings could be insistent on the point, refusing to talk or answer questions until a potential business partner made the first move.<ref name="SH" /> Persistence&mdash;to the point of pestering&mdash;was a favored tactic. Squibs continually asked for things that the owner had expressed no interest in parting with, hoping that the mark would eventually give in out of sheer annoyance.<ref name="UAA" />

The haggling process itself was more valued than any spoils obtained. In Squib reckoning, a good bout of bargaining let both sides think they were getting the better deal at least once. A key to Squib success was to involve as much complexity and as many individuals as possible: the more intricate a deal, the better, and a confused customer was a good customer.<ref name="SH" /> Squibs preferred to trade for things whose values were not easily comparable, thus preventing anyone from really knowing who got the best bargain.<ref name="SH" /> By involving several partners, any losses were spread out, and the chances that any one party felt any more than mildly ripped off were minimized.<ref name="GG4" /> Although the negotiations themselves could be quite intricate, the terms of the deal could preferably be completed quickly, without lengthy payments or interest&mdash;considered more the Ugors' style.<ref name="SH" />

[[File:Squib_MEAS.jpg|thumb|right|Squib traders operated shops across the galaxy.]]
Squib ideas of value differed from those of most other beings. Worth was determined by something called ''[[kRR value]]'', a concept not easily translatable. Gaining a great quantity of something or obtaining something novel was highly desirable.<ref name="SH" /> Squibs preferred to trade things they could see and touch; abstract commodities, such as information, were less attractive.<ref name="DC">{{LivingForce|Almas, Sweet Almas: Desert Cries}}</ref> ''Anything'' could be brought to the bargaining table, including a Squib's own offspring. The species' legends told of a mythical, idyllic [[junk heap of the ancients]].<ref name="H&R" />

A deal was a binding oath. Squibs went to great lengths to ensure their arrangements went through, and members of the species were incredibly loyal to their business partners, even accompanying them&mdash;saving their lives if need be&mdash;to help them complete their end of a bargain. Nevertheless, Squib interpretations of business arrangements could be fluid and subjective; many of their partners later found themselves wondering whether the Squibs were still adhering to the terms at all.<ref name="TG">''[[Tatooine Ghost]]''</ref> Nonetheless, the beings genuinely shunned deception and theft, so any apparent reneging was often perfectly justified in their own minds. For example, they believed that cheating was perfectly acceptable as long as they did not lie outright.<ref name="SH" /> The Squib [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Slythor]], for instance, often threw in a droid designated [[R4-B11]] with deals he made; what he kept secret was that the droid was programmed to kill the business partners and return with the goods Slythor had traded them.<ref name="The Official Star Wars Fact File 11">{{FactFile|11|AST 3-4|R3 & R4 Astromech Droids}}</ref> Despite such flightiness, many beings knew Squibs to be mostly honest;<ref name="GG4" /> in fact, members of the [[Morseerian/Legends|Morseerian]] species often preferred dealing with Squibs to other species.<ref name="UAA" />

===Language===
{{Quote|Us Squibs learn real good Basic. Study 'em up lots from examining plenty good garbage, you bet.|Spilferithimus-narlamos|<ref name="SH" />}}
Squibs read, wrote, and spoke a [[Language/Legends|language]] called [[Squibbian]]<ref name="UAA" /> or Squibbal.<ref name="Asc">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Ascension]]''</ref> The language developed from [[Old High Squibbian]], a tongue that remained in use as a secret form of communication for [[Spy/Legends|spies]] to convey the coordinates of trash dumps<ref name="SH" /> and for [[Merchant/Legends|traders]] to avoid being understood by those with whom they were bartering.<ref>''[[Tatooine Ghost]]'', mentions the trade language. {{DoD|Echoes of the Jedi}} shows that it is simply another name for Old High Squibbian</ref> The species reckoned [[Time/Legends|time]] using a measure known as the [[cergl-unit]].<ref name="SH" /> Squib names tended to be rather long, although the beings usually adopted shorter forms for use with non-Squibs. For example, the names Galaneever-marmalios, Meelawindemort, and Sleerinwilpher-remalior shortened to Galan, Meela, and Wilpher, respectively.<ref name="UAA" /> Other short Squib names included the masculine names Grees and Sligh, and the feminine names Emala, Muatisi, Pika, and Veeshu.<ref name="Asc" />

Members of the species had high-pitched voices.<ref name="Asc" /> Most spoke [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]], and, although some achieved fluency,<ref>See, for example, ''[[Tatooine Ghost]]'', the [[Star Wars: The Dark Nest Trilogy|''Dark Nest'' trilogy]], and ''[[Looking In: Memories|Memories]]''</ref> most Squibs' command of the tongue was less than perfect. Few Squibs could read and write the language.<ref name="UAA" /> They often had thick accents,<ref name="SH" /> and their knowledge of idiom could be quite limited. Determining what information Squibs were trying to convey could prove onerous:<ref name="GG4" /> they might speak too quickly, combine seemingly incongruous subjects in a single breath, or mention things that seemed of no relevance to the discussion at hand.<ref name="DC" /> Squibs peppered their Basic with unusual expressions, such as ''[[koovy]]'',<ref name="HNN Nowhere">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|47|regional/13314_2.html|Squibs Announce They're "Going Nowhere."}}</ref> and often ended sentences with "you bet."<ref name="Pablo92">{{Blog|pablog|92|Rookies: No Turning Back &mdash; Week Seven and Eight Annotations}}</ref> When bargaining, Squibs were meticulous about explaining terms, however. Trading with Squibs was a sure method of getting information from them.<ref name="GG4" /> Squib body language employed their unique physiology: their whiskers trembled to express indignation, their ears drooped to convey discomfort<ref name="Asc" /> and went back when alarmed,<ref name="Ap" /> and their hackles stood on end to show nervousness.<ref name="TTWS" />

===Institutions===
{{Quote|So, dealers with abridged decks, we of lofty Squib greet you in name of universal buddy-buddyness, irrespectful of differences in station, no less.|King Ebareebaveebeedee|<ref name="SH" />}}
[[File:Ebareebaveebeedee.jpg|thumb|left|upright|The Squib king was the nominal head of the Squib Polyanarchy.]]
Groups of related Squibs formed a family unit.<ref name="Asc" /> Beyond the immediate kin network, their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], [[Skor II]], was governed by the [[Squib Polyanarchy]], autonomous communities under the rule of a mostly hands-off [[King/Legends|king]].<ref name="DB Squib" /> In addition, all Squibs were employees of a species-wide corporation called the [[Squib Merchandising Consortium]],<ref name="GG4" /><ref name="SH" /> which held important contracts with [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] and planetary governments to collect, refurbish, and resell refuse. The degree of involvement varied;<ref name="GG4" /> at one extreme were individuals such as Squib [[Diplomat/Legends|diplomats]], recognizable by the ceremonial [[Fizz-Pop Cap (with foil cluster)]];<ref name="SH" /> at the other were independent traders.<ref name="GG4" /> The head of the Consortium was known as the [[Illustrious Chieftain of Junkyards]]. During the latter years of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and early years of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], a Squib named [[Ebareebaveebeedee]] served as both the Illustrious Chieftain and the Squib king. All Squibs were beholden to [[High Squibbian Law]], a system that, among other things, forbade the king from using the ceremonial items hanging from his robes<ref name="SH" /> and stipulated that possession was nine-hundred-and-ninety-nine one-thousandths of the law.<ref name="EOTJ">{{DoD|Echoes of the Jedi}}</ref> The Polyanarchy was historically apolitical,<ref name="UAA" /> although it supported the Galactic Republic during the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]]<ref name="HNN Nowhere" /> and signed a [[Unidentified Squib pact|pact of mutual support]] with the Alliance to Restore the Republic sometime between the battles of [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Yavin]] and [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Hoth]].<ref name="date">[[Scavenger Hunt (adventure)|''Scavenger Hunt'']] takes place at an unspecified point after the destruction of the first [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]], which occurred in [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]] according to ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'', and before the assignment of [[Carlist Rieekan/Legends|Carlist Rieekan]] to [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]], which occurred in [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]] according to ''The New Essential Chronology''</ref>

One major arm of the Consortium and a major Squib employer was the [[Squib Reclamation Fleet]].<ref name="H&R" /> Its vessels followed [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]] from one jump point to the next, collecting garbage jettisoned along the way.<ref name="SH" /> Squibs worked on the capital ships as garbage collectors and conveyed to the fleet the coordinates of dumps and any trade opportunities in the area.<ref name="GG4" /> The Reclamation Fleet was shadowed by vessels of the Squibs' rivals, the Ugors, who regularly swept in, attacked any Squib craft, and grabbed as much salvage as possible.<ref name="SH" />

===Technology===
{{Quote|Alien scavengers, identify selfs or face quick obliteration by awesome Squib weaponry, you bet.|A Squib aboard the ''Thrifty''|<ref name="SH" />}}
The Squibs had access to all aspects of [[Galaxy/Legends|galactic]] technology, although it differed from the standard in that it was often created from salvaged components refitted in ways the original makers never intended.<ref name="SH" /> Companies such as [[Fegegrish Heavy Industrials]] sold personal gear specifically designed for the Squib species, such as the shoulder-mounted [[Squib battering ram]],<ref name="Scum and Villainy sourcebook">[[Scum and Villainy (sourcebook)|''Scum and Villainy'']]</ref> which weakened obstructions at the molecular level.<ref name="UAA" /> The Squibs themselves refurbished scavenged items for resale on the galactic market; they could be quite successful at this endeavor when they returned such items to factory-like conditions.<ref name="TBHC">''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]''</ref> In contrast, Squib-designed inventions often proved a hard sell to other species. The [[C2-R4]] multipurpose droid flopped due to its poor aesthetics and bafflingly over-abundant functionality. Squib inventors rarely lost heart, however; a failed product simply afforded the chance to bargain with the creditors.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Droids">''[[The Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>

[[File:Squib_tensor_rifle.jpg|thumb|right|The Squib tensor rifle damaged its target with compressed waves of tractor energy.]]
Squibs excelled at [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]] technology.<ref name="GFT">''[[Galladinium's Fantastic Technology]]''</ref> Their tractor beams rivaled the best in the galaxy, and Squib [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] became experts at using them. For example, Squib [[needle ship]]s had no weaponry or [[Deflector shield/Legends|shields]], instead relying on ten tractor beams&mdash;rumored to be among the most powerful in the galaxy<ref name="The Official Star Wars Fact File 30">{{FactFile|30|TRA 1-4|Tractor Beams}}</ref>&mdash;for defense.<ref name="GG4" /> If attacked, the crew used quick and precise manipulations to erect a wall of garbage around the ship and hurl pieces of refuse at the enemy.<ref name="SH" /> The popular [[garbage grabber]] was a personal tractor beam with a claw at the end for gathering salvage from hard-to-reach places.<ref name="RR">''[[Rookies: Rendezvous]]''</ref> Squib [[Engineer/Legends|engineers]] developed whole weapons based on tractor beam technology. Called [[tensor weapon]]s, they attacked with invisible&mdash;but loud&mdash;compressed waves of tractor energy and disrupted the target's cells. [[Amberlandrax Armaments]] marketed a [[Tensor rifle|rifle]] of such design during the Galactic Civil War.<ref name="GFT" /> Squibs sometimes took advantage of the noisiness of such weapons to convince dismissive beings to pay attention to them.<ref name="TUR" />

Squib starshipwrights constructed spacecraft from second-hand materials. The main vessels of the Squib Reclamation Fleet were the tapered, fifty-meter needle ships, each crewed by twenty individuals.<ref name="SH" /> The fleet [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]] was for many years the ''[[Wholesale]]''.<ref name="H&R" /> Other important vessels were the Momships,<ref name="DB Squib" /> one of which was the personal vessel of the Squib king. Ebareebaveebeedee's vessel was the ''Thrifty''.<ref name="SH" /> Others traveled in [[Tramp freighter/Legends|tramp freighters]]<ref name="AA">''[[Alien Anthology]]''</ref> or [[Squib scout ship]]s, small craft armed with but a single tractor beam.<ref name="H&R" /> Some Squib craft were considered "[[Ugly/Legends|Uglies]]" similar to those employed by pirate groups.<ref name="P&P">''[[Pirates & Privateers]]''</ref>

==History==
===Evolution and early civilization===
{{Quote|Beware of smiling Squibs.|Old traders' saying|<ref name="DB Squib" />}}
[[File:UgorShip.jpg|thumb|left|A Squib needle ship (left) faces off with an Ugor vessel (right).]]
The Squibs evolved on Skor II, a small, dense [[Planet/Legends|world]] in the [[Squab system]],<ref name="AA" /> just west of the [[Rimma Trade Route/Legends|Rimma Trade Route]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> The planet possessed a diverse ecosystem, varied terrain, and vast resources spread far across its surface. Early tribes of Squibs thus were forced to travel from region to region to find necessities. Accumulating material goods became an ingrained part of the Squib psyche, leading some tribes to found small [[City/Legends|villages]]. Those who maintained their nomadic lifestyle took on the added role of merchants, trading foreign goods with their sedentary counterparts. Bargaining became a deep-seated part of Squib culture.<ref name="GG4" />

The Squibs advanced to the point of mass production and developed a peaceful, species-wide government called the Polyanarchy. Sometime before<ref name="ROTHC">{{TORcite|exp=rothc|type=crewskill|Scavenging|Urgent Recruitment}}</ref> [[3640 BBY]],<ref name="Date">{{TOR_updates|2.0}}</ref> a [[Dorcin]] trader discovered their world. After a spirited round of negotiations, the offworlder gained [[Ore/Legends|mineral]] rights to some frigid wastes, while the Squibs learned the intricacies of starship technology.<ref name="GG4" /> Shortly after the [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformation]], the Squib species had become well enough integrated into the galaxy to merit an entry in a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Book/Legends|training manual]], [[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force|''The Jedi Path'']], by the Jedi [[Academician|biologist]] [[Bowspritz]]. The researcher noted that Squibs had helped to get him out of trouble in the past, but that the experiences cost him a great deal of [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]]. Among marginalia added by other Jedi in one copy of the book, [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] noted that he considered them thieves.<ref name="TJP" />

The Squibs' natural curiosity and mastery of haggling helped them to carve out a niche as interstellar garbage collectors and scavengers.<ref name="GG4" /> While Squib settlers colonized other planets,<ref name="SIII">{{LivingForce|For Every Action: Strike III}}</ref> Squib companies signed contracts to haul rubbish from populous worlds while other corporations refurbished the junk for resale.<ref name="GG4" /> Skor II became a prosperous trade world with a major population center at [[Metrobig City]]. Sometime before [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]], the planet joined the Galactic Republic.<ref name="HNN Nowhere" />

Meanwhile, the Squibs' activities put them in direct competition with another scavenger species: the Ugors. Over time, the species developed a fraught antagonism,<ref name="GG4" /> practically to the point of war. The Squibs came to regard the Ugors as their hereditary foes,<ref name="SH" /> and the Ugors made the Squibs de facto [[Demon/Legends|demons]] in their religion of trash worship.<ref name="SH" />

===Reign of Ebareebaveebeedee===
{{Quote|Our ultrastrong loyalties and royalties to Republicness and whatever it may stand for will not let splitty-types coax-haggle Squibbish into leaving, no matter the size of the haggleprize.|King Ebareebaveebeedee|<ref name="HNN Nowhere" />}}
[[File:Mace_Windu_statue_on_Skor_II.jpg|thumb|right|upright|King Ebareebaveebeedee unveiled a statue of Mace Windu after the Battle of Skor II.]]
Sometime before [[40 BBY/Legends|40 BBY]], Ebareebaveebeedee became king of the Polyanarchy. His reign proved something of a golden age. Under his initiative, the species struck deals with various galactic interests to place Squibs aboard capital ships as garbage laborers. To many observers, they were little better than [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]], although it was understood that they were allowed to keep any scrap that caught their eye. In the eyes of the Squib government, Squibs so employed were embedded spies, whose job was to communicate the coordinates of capital-ship garbage dumps to the Squib Reclamation Fleet.<ref name="SH" />

Despite overtures from the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], Ebareebaveebeedee enthusiastically supported the Galactic Republic during the Separatist Crisis, declaring that his people were "going nowhere" and that the Jedi were "koovy."<ref name="HNN Nowhere" /> In month 15 of [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]], [[Metrobig Interplanetary Blastport]] was seized by the Separatists. [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]]<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> and [[Clone Marshal Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Cody/Legends|Cody]]<ref name="Labyrinth of Evil">''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''</ref> led Republic forces to drive away the [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] and recapture the [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] in the [[Battle of Skor II]].<ref name="NEC" /> Ebareebaveebeedee erected a [[Bronzium/Legends|bronzium]] [[Statue of Mace Windu|statue]] in honor of Windu and named him "[[Big Time Hero of Beyond-Squib Eliteness]]."<ref name="HNN Battle">{{InsiderCite|69|Republic HoloNet News Core Edition 14:9:01}}</ref> The Squibs found their homeworld in uncontrolled territory for the remainder of the war.<ref name="TEA" /> Still, during the conflict, Squib scavengers cleaned up after battles; the Jedi [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] thus considered Squibs to be good sources of intelligence on Separatist movements.<ref name="TJP" />

After the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the Squibs suffered a minor hiccup over the salvage of orbital wrecks.<ref name="Republic HoloNet News Special Inaugural Edition 16:5:241">"[[Republic HoloNet News Special Inaugural Edition 16:5:241]]."</ref> The incident was followed by an even graver threat: early in the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]], the Squibs found themselves elbowed out by their rivals, the Ugors, as much of the galaxy came to rely upon Ugor waste disposal services.<ref name="GG4" /> The Ugors even secured an exclusive Imperial license not only to collect Imperial garbage dumps in deep space but also to accept dumps from Imperial ships visiting the Ugors' home [[Star system/Legends|star system]], Paradise.<ref name="CSWE III 277">{{CSWECite|III|277|Ugor}}</ref> Ebareebaveebeedee countered by securing permission to allow Squib sanitation workers aboard Imperial vessels, a ploy that perpetuated his network of informants.<ref name="GG4" /> The Squibs were forced to rely even more on their spy network; armed with its intelligence, their craft could swoop in and snap up as much garbage as possible before the Ugors arrived to chase them away.<ref name="SH" />

The Squib King largely kept his people out of the Galactic Civil War<ref name="UAA" /> after its outbreak in [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]],<ref name="CSWE I 143">{{CSWECite|I|143|Corellian Treaty}}</ref> and the species traded and dealt with members of both the Galactic Empire and the Alliance to Restore the Republic. [[Alliance Intelligence/Legends|Alliance]] and [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]] tried to track Squib vessels to the bases of their enemies, but the species made sure to secure the secrecy of their markets.<ref name="UAA" /> The species profited from the galactic conflict by scavenging equipment from battle sites, repairing it, and reselling it; several military-issue [[Arakyd Aerodynes, Inc.|Arakyd]] [[74-Z speeder bike/Legends|74-Z]] [[Speeder bike/Legends|speeder bikes]] made their way to the civilian market in this way.<ref name="TBHC" />

Sometime between [[0 ABY/Legends|0]] and [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]],<ref name="date" /> the Squibs hit their nadir. Their intelligence revealed that the Ugors had obtained a [[Gravity well projector/Legends|gravity well projector]] with which they were bringing order to the junk in their home system. The greater organization granted the [[Ugor salvage fleet]] greater efficiency and drew new customers to both dump their garbage<ref name="SH" /> and seek rare pieces of flotsam and jetsam.<ref name="GG4" /> The king thus reneged on his earlier policy of neutrality: he made a deal with a group of Rebel operatives to provide information on the location of an Imperial ship they [[Mission to destroy Elusive|sought]] in exchange for the projector. When the Rebels and a Squib diplomat named [[Spilferithimus-narlamos]] removed the contraption, the Paradise system fell back into disarray. Ebareebaveebeedee then declared a pact of mutual support between the Squibs and the Alliance.<ref name="Scavenger Hunt">[[Scavenger Hunt (adventure)|''Scavenger Hunt'']]</ref> By [[137 ABY]], Skor II had fallen within territory controlled by the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Krayt]] as part of his [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="TEA" />

==Squibs in the galaxy==
{{Quote|Secret agent Dono to Momship. Hope you enjoying plenty big treasure dump. Plenty good stuff left on big-ship, you bet. Have place-numbers for next big-ship stop. Will transmit in super-secret Squib code. Starting now.|[[Dono (Squib)|Dono]]|<ref name="SH" />}}
[[File:SluissiSnivvianSpinerSquib-UAA.jpg|thumb|left|Squibs freely mingled with species across the galaxy.]]
Although a few held mundane jobs, such as [[Pilot/Legends|flying]] [[Air taxi/Legends|air taxis]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]],<ref name="INV" /> garbage was everywhere, and Squibs were anywhere the garbage was.<ref name="GG4" /> Capital ships contracted Squib sanitation workers to handle onboard refuse. A telltale sign that Squibs were aboard was that ejected trash had been stripped of potentially valuable parts.<ref name="RES">''[[Rebellion Era Sourcebook]]''</ref> Many galactic citizens came to regard the diminutive beings as no more than laborers, an idea that persisted well into the days of the [[New Jedi Order]].<ref name="UAA" /> Especially during the days of the Empire, Squib garbage workers kept a low profile and avoided contact with their employers; others broke their contracts due to mistreatment. Rebel Alliance operatives cultivated disaffected Squibs to gain valuable logistical and operational intelligence about Imperial vessels.<ref name="RES" /> In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], undercover Alliance operatives were subcontracted by the Squib [[Jeremos]] to work aboard the [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] [[Indomitable (Imperial I-class)|''Indomitable'']]. They used their position to gain access to sensitive areas of the ship and further their mission.<ref name="RES" /> Squib salvagers occasionally hired non-Squibs to help them in their duties.<ref name="ROTHC" />

Some Squibs were [[Fringer/Legends|fringers]],<ref name="UAA" /> scavenging on a single planet. For instance, [[Squeerie]] led a team on [[Almas]] around [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] and helped a group of agents working for the [[Human/Legends|Human]] Jedi Master [[Lanius Qel-Bertuk]] to find his lost [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] counterpart, [[Kirlocca]].<ref name="DC">{{LivingForce|Almas, Sweet Almas: Desert Cries}}</ref> Sometime after [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]] at the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], members of Squeerie's group, led by [[Jiminaldo-mabbramsti]], or Jimi, encountered agents of Jedi Master [[Denia]] while fighting with a group of Ugors over the salvage of a [[7-A39|damaged droid]] in the ruins of [[Almas Academy]].<ref name="EOTJ" />

{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Echoes of the Jedi}}
The offworlders mediated the dispute.<ref name="EOTJ" />
{{Endgame}}

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], a number of worlds in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] and the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]] were found to be infested with [[Stone mite/Legends|stone mites]]. The [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] containing such planets were usually evacuated of all inhabitants, so great was the fear of spreading these creatures to the rest of the galaxy. Worlds thus abandoned became tempting locations for various [[Scavenger/Legends|scavengers]], such as the Squibs. They were also known to search stone mite–ravaged worlds for undamaged equipment. Although Squib reclamation teams were usually canny enough to avoid exporting stone mites to other worlds, many other scavengers were either unaware of or indifferent to the problem.<ref name="RA">{{Wizards|url=starwars/article.asp?x=sw20011115a_slug&c=rpg|text=Rescued Aliens: Swamp Slug and Stone Mite}}</ref>

However, immediately thereafter, a group of [[Dark Lizard]]s attacked all parties.<ref name="EOTJ" /> [[Maja]] was a Squib who purchased salvage rights to a waste field on the [[Third moon of Kothlis|third moon]] of [[Kothlis/Legends|Kothlis]] around [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]]. He was trapped in a [[Tech 4 PDV|Plexus Droid Vessel]] and soon found himself facing a group of adventurers who needed information from the conveyance. As a good Squib trader, Maja gave up his would-be personal craft for the right price.<ref name="SOTEPG">{{WEGCite|story=Operation: Recovery|book=Shadows of the Empire Planets Guide}}</ref>

[[File:Squib_in_asteroid_hopper.png|thumb|right|upright|Squib spacers collected interstellar trash for refurbishment and resale.]]
Other Squibs took to a life as spacers. Some acted as [[Scout/Legends|scouts]],<ref name="UAA" /> passively scanning deep space for interesting junk, while others tracked vessels to reclaim their garbage dumps.<ref name="GG4" /> Squib vessels joined the wreckage of the [[Hoth asteroid field/Legends|Hoth asteroid field]] while attempting to salvage the remains of the [[Mugaari]] pirate [[Icanis Tsur]] 's [[80-Vag|ship]].<ref name="Galactic Gazetteer: Hoth and the Greater Javin">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20040325web|text=Galactic Gazetteer: Hoth and the Greater Javin|int=Galactic Gazetteer: Hoth and the Greater Javin}}</ref>

{{GameMechanics|legends=1|New Recruits and Rebel Guns}}
During the Galactic Civil War, a [[Unidentified Squib spacer|Squib spacer]] was present at the [[Cantina/Legends|bar]] called [[the Maze]] when a group of would-be Rebel Alliance operatives fled Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]].<ref name="NRRG" />
{{Endgame}}

In [[13 ABY/Legends|13 ABY]], the crew of a [[Unidentified Squib prospector vessel|Squib prospector vessel]] was detained on the [[Quarantine Enforcement Cruiser]] ''[[Lycoming]]''.<ref name="POT">''[[Planet of Twilight]]''</ref> A [[Unidentified Squib tourist|Squib tourist]] in [[Piringiisi]] on [[Sullust/Legends|Sullust]] survived a [[Dianoga/Legends|dianoga]] attack, alerting the authorities to the presence of the predator in the mud pits there.<ref name="Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds">''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]''</ref> Circa [[24 ABY/Legends|24 ABY]], a [[Unidentified Squib salvage scow|Squib salvage scow]] recovered artifacts from the ruins of the planet [[Byss/Legends|Byss]], including a copy of the book ''The Jedi Path''.<ref name="TJP" />

Squib traders traveled to even the most remote and secretive locations to sell reconditioned goods, prompting many top-secret installations to completely rethink their security procedures upon the arrival of such unexpected company.<ref name="UAA" /> They were one of the few species from the known galaxy to have established any significant presence in the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]], and their language served as one of the many ''lingua franca'' used in that area of space. Indeed, [[Unidentified Squib scout|one Squib scout]] made first contact for the galactic scavengers with a [[Unidentified Chiss explorers|pair of explorers]] of the [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] species.<ref name="TUR" /> The species was so well established that Squibs were among the many targets presented by the [[Hologram/Legends|holographic]] shooting range of Almas Academy.<ref name="EOTJ" /> A Squib named [[Kwilper]] wandered from spaceport to spaceport selling pieces of art he had fashioned from salvaged junk,<ref name="H&R" /> and in 3 ABY, a Squib named [[Veeter]] found himself stranded on [[Dalicron-4]], desperate to repair his ship and return to his wandering lifestyle.<ref name="COL" /> Occasionally, roving Squib traders obtained goods whose value even they could not imagine. [[Unidentified Squib|One]] found himself the center of a bidding war among parties interested in a data storage unit with an important decryption program.<ref name="Alien Adventures">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20011101c|text=Alien Adventures|int=Alien Adventures}}</ref>

Squibs opened second-hand shops in spaceport towns.<ref name="GG4" /> Around [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], [[Macemillian-winduarté]] helped run [[Jawa Traders]], a droid shop on the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="GG7" /> The gray-furred Squib had to deal with thugs hired by [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] to collect protection money from him. At one point, a group of spacers helped him resist such a shakedown; Macemillian-winduarté loaned the offworlders a [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeder]] in gratitude.<ref name="TMSBCL">{{WEGCite|story=There's Many a Slip Betwixt Cup and Lip|book=Mos Eisley Adventure Set}}</ref> In [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]], [[Arrejis Mellaha]] operated [[Serooin's Gear]] on the [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]]' world [[Betha II]].<ref name="CS">{{JournalCite|8|Counterstrike (Adventure Journal)}}</ref> In 13 ABY, [[Sheebareevadee]] ran [[Sheebareevadee's Emporium of Interstellar Goods]] on the planet [[Gamorr/Legends|Gamorr]].<ref name="MiS">{{JournalCite|14|Murder in Slushtime}}</ref> Other Squib traders included [[Unidentified Squib trader (Asation)|one]] on the planet [[Asation]]<ref name="GE">{{JournalCite|8|The Gree Enclave}}</ref> and [[Unidentified Squib trader (Kabal)|another]] on the planet [[Kabal/Legends|Kabal]].<ref name="FP" />

[[File:Chiss-squib-tur.jpg|thumb|left|Squib scouts penetrated even the Unknown Regions, where they made contact with representatives of the Chiss Ascendancy.]]
Other Squibs took up the life of [[Scoundrel/Legends|scoundrels]].<ref name="UAA" /> Their ranks included petty thieves, such as the pickpocket-turned-Rebel [[Smileredon-Verdont]],<ref name="RR" /><ref name="RNTB" /> forgers, like the [[Unidentified Squib forgers|two Squibs]] employed by the [[Sljee/Legends|Sljee]] [[Jeseej]] on Coruscant,<ref name="C&TCW">''[[Coruscant and the Core Worlds]]''</ref> [[Information broker/Legends|infochants]], such as [[Burnout (space station)|Burnout]] [[Space station/Legends|space station's]] [[Blasnic]],<ref name="M">{{LivingForce|Looking In: Memories}}</ref> and full-fledged crime lords, such as Slythor, who controlled salvage operations on the junk planet [[Korad]].<ref name="OE" /> [[Unidentified Squib thieves|Four Squib thieves]] were tasked by the Human Rebel operative [[Quip Fargil]] on the planet [[Sriluur/Legends|Sriluur]] to steal components from an [[Immobilizer 418 Interdictor-class Heavy Cruiser|Interdictor cruiser]] to help upgrade the [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] of the [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']].<ref name="MF">[[Millennium Falcon (novel)|''Millennium Falcon'']]</ref>

The family unit of [[Emala]], [[Grees]], and [[Sligh]]<ref name="Asc" /> were a trio of scoundrels who had dealings with the Human [[Solo family/Legends|Solo family]] over the years. In [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], they were working as [[Information broker/Legends|information brokers]], selling data to the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. They teamed up with the Solos to obtain the [[Painting/Legends|painting]] ''[[Killik Twilight]]'', which contained hidden data sensitive to the New Republic.<ref name="TG" /> They later worked with members of the criminal organization known as the [[Invisible Shell]], but when their patsy, the [[Jenet/Legends|Jenet]] [[Ludlo Lebauer]], learned of their scheme, he [[Carbon-freezing/Legends|froze]] Grees in [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]]. The Squibs manipulated the Solos into helping them rescue their companion on the [[Casino/Legends|casino]] planet [[Pavo Prime/Legends|Pavo Prime]].<ref name="TTWS" /> Following the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the three were still selling artwork, and their organization had grown to include Emala's children, [[Krafte]] and [[Seneki]], as well as Squib [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]].<ref name="TSW">''[[Dark Nest III: The Swarm War]]''</ref> By [[44 ABY]], the trio had found work with the Human [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Natasi Daala]], the former [[Chief of State (Galactic Alliance)|Chief of State]] of the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]], who sent them<ref name="Ap">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse]]''</ref> to become test subjects for [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Tol Getelles]], who was conducting trials of a [[Unidentified droch serum|serum]], derived from a creature known as the [[Droch/Legends|droch]], that had the ability to restore youth to its taker.<ref name="Asc" /> During their tenure with the Human [[Officer/Legends|officer]], the information brokers became familiar with Getelles' hidden [[Laboratory/Legends|laboratory]] complex, which was masked as a [[Mine/Legends|mine]] called the [[Moon Maiden]] on the mining moon [[Hagamoor 3]].<ref name="Ap" /> There they discovered Daala's plot to oust Head of State [[Jagged Fel]] of the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] from power. The Squibs' involvement was revealed when they crossed paths with the Solos later that year. In return for information about the experiments, the Solos granted the Squibs safe passage to Coruscant.<ref name="Asc" /> On the galactic [[Capital/Legends|capital]], the Squibs turned over a stolen vial of the serum to Fel under threat of arrest.<ref name="Asc" /> They next took a job for the Human [[Lydea Pagorski]], an Imperial [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] who served as Daala's campaign manager in a race against Fel. The Squibs led Pagorski to Getelles' abandoned Moon Maiden base, where she set up a campaign headquarters. Things turned sour when Pagorski revealed herself to be a monstrous [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] entity known as [[Abeloth]], intent only on drawing a constant stream of victims into the base to feed off their fear and anguish.<ref name="Ap" /> Meanwhile, the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] tracked the Squibs to the base in his hunt for a pair of scientists who had manufactured a [[Nanovirus|nanokiller]] tailored to his genetic makeup. While three other Squibs remained with Pagorski and enslaved workers in a fire bulkhead,<ref name="Ap" /> Sligh fled into hiding upon Fett's appearance. He was later discovered by the former [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Tahiri Veila]], who interrogated him through the Force and discovered the Squibs' dealings with Pagorski. Soon, the Squibs in the fire bulkhead came under attack from the Human Jedi and the Mandalorian bounty hunter, whom she had rescued.<ref name="Ap" /> The pair of Humans then defeated Abeloth in the chamber beyond.<ref name="Ap" />

A few Squibs had a talent for [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. Some [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] members of the species had no knowledge of their gifts and remained on Skor II,<ref name="AA" /> but others were trained as Jedi. A popular series of children's stories from the time of the Republic focused on a roguish [[Squib Jedi]] who was rumored to be based on a real individual.<ref name="UAA" /> The series went to several volumes; the third was titled ''[[Busteromuchmacho and the Vermillion Shadow]]''.<ref name="EOTJ" /> Years later, in [[35 ABY/Legends|35 ABY]], a [[Unidentified Squib Jedi|Squib Jedi]] was training at the [[Jedi Academy (Ossus)|Jedi Academy]] of the planet [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]].<ref name="TJK">''[[Dark Nest I: The Joiner King]]''</ref> A small number of Squib [[Noble/Legends|nobles]] plied the spacelanes.<ref name="TUR" />

More than 220 years before the Battle of Yavin, a [[Unidentified Squib vessel|Squib vessel]] crash landed on the planet [[Holador]]. The survivors broadcasted a distress signal and hunkered down to be rescued, to no avail. When their equipment failed, they were forced to revert to a primitive lifestyle. Over seven generations, the Squibs took to worshiping their [[Comm unit/Legends|comm relay]] as a Holy Icon and hoping for the day offworlders would once again return them to the [[Star/Legends|stars]]. A [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] bounty hunter named [[Kelyan]] tried to convince the village that a group of visiting adventurers was dangerous.<ref name="SIII" />

{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Strike III}}
Nevertheless, the village elder, [[Alexem]], was convinced that she was manipulating the tribe.<ref name="SIII" />
{{Endgame}}

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Staging tip: If you ever need to completely diffuse a tense argument scene, have a Squib look directly at 'camera,' like on panel 3. It works like a charm.|Pablo Hidalgo|<ref name="Pablo89">{{Blog|pablog|89|Rookies: No Turning Back - Month 1 Annotations}}</ref>}}
[[File:Rookies.jpg|thumb|right|upright|The ''Rookies: Rendezvous'' webstrip features the Squib character Smileredon-Verdont.]]
The Squibs were introduced by [[Brad Freeman]] in the [[West End Games]] adventure [[Scavenger Hunt (adventure)|''Scavenger Hunt'']], published in [[1989]]. The story sends a group of Rebel characters after the Imperial ship [[Elusive (transport)|''Elusive'']], the location of which is known only to the Squib king, Ebareebaveebeedee, and his crew.<ref name="SH" /> Later that year, [[Troy Denning]] gave the species a more complete write-up in ''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]''. The book indicates that they were intended as a sort of comic-relief species that, unlike [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]], could be encountered anywhere in the galaxy and interact with characters on a more technologically level playing field. West End's Squibs are more dexterous than the average species, but they are slightly restricted in intelligence, strength, and technical aptitude.<ref name="GG4" /> The [[Wizards of the Coast]] version of the species, detailed in both ''[[Alien Anthology]]'' ([[2001]]) and ''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]'' ([[2003]]), also has high agility, now coupled with lower-than-average common sense and perceptive abilities.<ref name="UAA" /><ref name="AA" /> With the change to the Saga edition of the Wizards' system, Squibs suffer a penalty to strength, but a bonus to their agility. They gain the additional ability to retry any attempt to manipulate technology.<ref name="TUR" /> Several sources summarize material from these books without adding new information on the species.<ref>See ''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe]]'', the ''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', and ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

The information above assumes that encounters with Squibs in various role-playing scenarios follow the most profitable course for the player characters. Nevertheless, several alternatives are possible. For instance, in the [[1996]] adventure ''[[New Recruits and Rebel Guns]]'', the encounter between a Rebel Alliance player character and a Squib spacer in a bar called the Maze is offered only as a possibility and is not integral to the overall plot.<ref name="NRRG" /> In the [[2005]] adventure ''[[For Every Action: Strike III|Strike III]]'', the Squib leader Alexem and his tribe may decide to attack the player characters if they fail to convince him that they do not have hostile intentions.<ref name="SIII" /> Finally, in [[2008]]'s ''[[Echoes of the Jedi]]'', the player characters have the option of ignoring the dispute between Jiminaldo-mabbramsti and his Ugor rivals, but doing so nets them a smaller reward.<ref name="EOTJ" />

Denning has featured the Squib characters Emala, Grees, and Sligh prominently in five novels and one short story,<ref>See ''[[Tatooine Ghost]]'', the [[Star Wars: The Dark Nest Trilogy|''Dark Nest'' trilogy]], ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse]]'', and "[[The Trouble with Squibs]]."</ref> and the trio has appeared in ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Ascension]]'', by [[Christie Golden]], as well. [[Pablo Hidalgo]], another ''[[Star Wars]]'' author, has expressed his affection for the Squibs in his blog.<ref name="Pablo53">{{Blog|pablog|53|Rookies: Rendezvous -- Week Five Annotations}}</ref> One of his players portrayed a Squib character named Smileredon-Verdonté in a campaign of ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' that Hidalgo refereed. The character&mdash;with a slightly modified name&mdash;later featured in ''[[Heroes & Rogues]]'' ([[1995]]) and as a regular in the ''Rookies'' webstrips.<ref name="Blog-pablog|55">{{Blog|pablog|55|Rookies: Rendezvous -- Week Seven Annotations}}</ref><ref name="Blog-pablog|88">{{Blog|pablog|88|Origin of the Rookies}}</ref> Hidalgo's chronicle of the Battle of Skor II explains why a Squib character in ''[[Galaxy Guide 7: Mos Eisley]]'' is named "Mace Windu," the same as the Jedi character played by [[Samuel L. Jackson]] in the [[Prequel trilogy|prequel films]]: the name&mdash;and variants&mdash;has appeared in [[George Lucas]]'s notes and drafts for the ''Star Wars'' saga since [[1973]].<ref name="The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref> According to Hidalgo's article, the Squib (whose full name is Macemillian-winduarté), was simply named for the Jedi hero who saved his home planet. Although Denning's Squib characters tend to speak standard Basic, Hidalgo's speak in what he describes as "Squibberish," a babbling, imprecise version of Basic punctuated by Squibbian words like "koovy."<ref name="Pablo53" /><ref name="Pablo89" />

The species has caused some problems in ''Star Wars'' fiction. For example, the word is misspelled ''Squibb'' in the ''[[Star Wars Adventure Journal]]'' articles "[[Murder in Slushtime]]"<ref name="MiS" /> and "[[The Gree Enclave]]."<ref name="GE" /> The novels ''[[Shield of Lies]]''<ref name="SOL">''[[Shield of Lies]]''</ref> and [[Shatterpoint/Legends|''Shatterpoint'']] write the species' name in lowercase. [[The Official Star Wars Fact File 138|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' 138]] claims that the Squibs hail from the Paradise system along with their rivals, the Ugors.<ref name="The Official Star Wars Fact File 138">{{FactFile|138|WAS 1-4|Waste Disposal}}</ref> More recent sources, such as ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', contradict the notion,<ref name="The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia III-159">{{CSWECite|III|159|Skor II}}</ref> so the ''Fact File'' seems to be in error. "[[HoloNet Waystation (article)|HoloNet Waystation]]," a non-licensed roleplaying adventure in [[Challenge 74|''Challenge'' 74]], suggests that Tatooine was too remote for Squibs to visit.<ref name="HoloNet Waystation article">{{ChallengeCite|74|HoloNet Waystation (article)}}</ref> The assertion contradicts the presence of Macemillian-winduarté living there as a trader, as established in ''Galaxy Guide 7: Mos Eisley''<ref name="GG7" /> and the short story "[[Spare Parts (short story)|Spare Parts]]."<ref name="SP" /> Sources are ambiguous as to the relationship between the Squib species and the Squib battering ram. ''[[Galladinium's Fantastic Technology]]'' describes the battering ram as part of its write-up for the Squib species as an example of something available to members of the species.<ref name="UAA" /> However, in ''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]'', the in-universe narrator, bounty hunter [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]], explains that the device was named ''for'' the Squibs&mdash;not designed by them&mdash;due to their penchant for getting into places they were not supposed to be.<ref name="TBHC" />
